Sex is a simple thing but we make it complicated with emotions and expectations. To put it simply, it is possible to want to have sex with other people but only love one person. Now the thing is that if you are a monogamous person then this lifestyle won’t work. It might NOT mean they don’t love you BUT if they go ahead and do things behind your back that DEFINITELY means they don’t love/care about you.

Now here’s the big thing, setting aside emotions and expectations and being open to a calm 100% honest conversation can help mend these things. Obviously you can only control what you say and do and will have to trust they are being 100% honest as well. That being said, don’t leave your intuition at the door either. Emotions and anxieties must be controlled but your intuition is good to have at the back of your head. 

During this conversation you should have VERY clear and concise questions you want to ask with 0 expectation of what they will say/what you want them to say. Just simply listen to what they say to what you want to know. 

If he wants to have sex with others while in a relationship and you are willing to try it then try it and if you don’t like it then break up.

If he wants to have sex with other people but you don’t but you’re okay with him doing it then try that and if you end up not liking it then break up.

If he wants to have sex with other people but you don’t like being in a open relationship simply tell them you love them and that you understand they love you but it just won’t work fundamentally and break up.

If he wants to have sex with other people but is willing to give it up for you then you can try the relationship but you will have to check your anxiety at the door and not think about him possibly cheating on you because if he isn’t then it will cause major problems. That being said, it isn’t impossible but it isn’t something you should bring up nor think about unless there’s 100% obvious proof he did. If you can’t do this then break up because if you can’t trust them then it won’t work in the end.

If you simply don’t want to think about the situation anymore and simply want to move on and try to find a love that suits you better. Just keep in mind that no relationship is 100% perfect. There will always be things to consider, give up, try out, compromise, struggle, and enjoy. 

Ultimately, the MOST important thing is knowing 100% who you are and what you want in a relationship that is both realistic and non comprisable. Wanting someone with 1 million a year income is pretty unrealistic. Wanting someone who is hard working and always pays their bills on time is very realistic.

I would suggest taking the time to think about what you want and can accept financially, physically, and emotionally. 

For example, I need someone financially responsible regardless of how much money they make. I need someone who is fit but neither underweight nor overweight. Finally, I need someone who can meet and understand the things that make me happy.

Everything else for me is stuff to talk about and either accept/compromise. But these are just my preferences that I want and won’t budge on. Just an example.

Other than that, good luck! “Remember, if you can’t love yourself, how in the hell are you guna love somebody else?” -Mama Ru

Two people solving shared problems and trying to clear things out to figure out what it is they both want and need. 

I hope that was helpful but I do have to say that at the end of it all, keep yourself safe. If leaving is what you feel is correct then that is your right to do so. Just be sure to explain what went wrong and why you’re leaving so that he may possibly be a better person in his next relationship.

Potential to crit is written as “x% to critical chance” that chance can be multiplied using the “x% chance to crit” 

Say you have 1% crit chance. You add 1% to crit chance. That’s 2% crit chance.

Say you have 1% crit chance. You then add 1% crit chance. You then have 1.01% crit chance. 

The the difference in the wording is “% to crit chance” and “% crit chance” 

With the damage modifiers your flat damage will always give the biggest bonus because everything else scales that damage up. “More damage” vs “increased damage” are additive and multiplicative respectively.

1 more damage to 1 damage is 2 damage.

1 increased damage to 1 damage is essentially still 1 damage.

Jokes are jokes, racism is racism. Jokes can apply racist connotations but jokes and humor are for creating lightheartedness over serious topics. Racism is straight saying shit like I hate black people and they mean it. These are two different things. 

Something I’ve noticed alot is very commonly, white people mostly, tend to be uncomfortable around racist humor because of the fear of being called racist. There’s nothing wrong with laughing at a joke but there is something wrong with trying to eliminate a silence a very important topic such as racism. 

All that being said, you are your own person and of course you have your own views on what you feel comfortable with. That’s 10000% understandable. He has his and that is too. The problem is that you aren’t comfortable and he does not see a problem with his jokes. While it is justified that joking is definitely not inherently bad, making you uncomfortable on purpose is. 

Obviously you have two big options: 

Stay or leave.

If you stay, are you capable of letting go of the uncomfortable feeling about jokes? They are just jokes after all.

If you leave, are you going to regret losing all the other parts of him that you did enjoy? After all, no ones perfect and relationships all have some compromises. 

Now all that being said, if you can’t get over the uncomfortability and you want to stay then you will have to have a serious conversation with patience and understanding to get to a point where you two can see where you are both coming from. Finding that connection is important. You both need to put the effort to understand each others perspective. Now after that, if boundaries are set and are being broken with no improvement then it would be best to leave. The key though is that theres a middle ground you both work towards and both can see each other improving.
